title: Earliest Possible Day of Full Bloom
summary: You are given n flower seeds, each requiring a specific number of days to plant and grow.
statement: You are given n flower seeds, each requiring a specific number of days to plant and grow. The plantTime array specifies the number of full days needed to plant each seed, and the growTime array specifies the number of full days needed for each seed to grow after being completely planted. You can plant one seed per day but must complete the planting before the seed can begin to grow. The goal is to determine the earliest possible day on which all seeds will have bloomed, considering any order of planting.
constraints: The arrays are equally sized with positive durations.
Only one seed can be planted at a time; growth occurs in parallel after planting completes.
Return the earliest day when every seed has bloomed.
hints: If two adjacent seeds have grow times a<b, planting b first cannot delay the later of their bloom days.
Sort seeds by descending grow time, accumulate planting time, and track completion plus grow time.
Repeated adjacent exchanges place longer growth first without worsening the objective, proving the greedy order optimal.
editorial: Repeated adjacent exchanges place longer growth first without worsening the objective, proving the greedy order optimal.

tests.explanation: Planting in grow-time order three, two, one yields all blooms by day nine.
Prioritizing the two longest grow times produces full bloom on day nine.
